title: Manual therapy
what: The doctor uses their hands to work on your muscles, joints, and spine: stretching, relaxing, and gently restoring movement.
why: For back, neck, and joint pain and stiffness, after an exam and scans, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: a session usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; the course is usually several sessions
tell_doctor: Where it hurts and for how long
Any numbness or weakness in your arms or legs
Osteoporosis, or past spine injuries or surgery
High blood pressure, or if you are pregnant

prepare.title: Scans
prepare.text: Bring X-rays, MRI scans, and reports. Without them, the doctor may not start.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come right after a big meal.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: The doctor asks questions and looks at your scans
Your movement, strength, and feeling are checked
Joints are gently stretched and moved
Sometimes there is a short click in a joint
At the end, you get advice and exercises
feel: There should be no strong pain. Tell the doctor right away
Afterward, a mild ache for 1 to 2 days can happen
after: Do not lift heavy things on the day of the session
Do the exercises the doctor gave you
If the pain gets worse, talk to your doctor
red_flags: Numbness or weakness in an arm or leg, severe dizziness, or trouble speaking after a session: call emergency services

faq.q: Do I need scans before manual therapy?
faq.a: Usually yes. They help the doctor know what is safe and what is not.

faq.q: Does a click mean a vertebra was put back?
faq.a: No. It is a sound from a joint as it moves. Vertebrae do not pop out like that.

reminders.text: Manual therapy tomorrow. Bring your scans and reports, and wear comfortable clothes.
